case_evidence.description: Frozen Python 1.2 public src/eyetrajectoriespy/plotting.py::plot_fpca_cross_validation. Source-scientific native strict mode is explicitly optional.

Native actual FPCA held-out reconstruction cross-validation result and finite per-fold integrated RMSE with source n_components/fold labels; source-ordered summary computes observed fold mean and standard error. Strict mode rejects arbitrary Python objects, nonnative R dataframes and negative/undefined source errorbars.

Native etr_summarise_fpca_cross_validation uses actual held-out fold integrated RMSE, retains candidate component counts, fold mean, source sample SD/sqrt(n_folds) standard error, and constructs exact source errorbar coordinates mean±SE, marker o and capsize=3. Pinned Python 1.2 summary from pandas groupby and public Matplotlib Axes.errorbar line x/y and one errorbar container compared on the same native fold_errors table; exact-head differential execution pending.

Strict rejects unknown class or incomplete/nonfinite source folds, negative/NaN SE, malformed component counts and nonlogical mode. Native base R plot errors and Python object-injection TypeError classes are not fully reproduced.

Python Matplotlib Axes with one ErrorbarContainer, marker o and capsize 3. Native strict source-scientific record exposes exact x component counts, per-count RMSE y, fold standard error and lower/upper errorbar positions and artist settings, while default R mode continues returning unchanged native CV summary dataframe. Live Matplotlib Axes identity and pixel-perfect rendered caps remain unimplemented.

Descriptive held-out integrated reconstruction RMSE across retained functional principal component counts, with sampling variation among observed CV folds. The SE bars are fold-level descriptive dispersion, not a bootstrap confidence interval or automatic model-selection claim.
